QuestionStmt.S: What is the IUPAC name of the compound $\mathrm{CH_3CH=CHCH=CHCOOH}$?

Solution.S:
The compound is $\mathrm{CH_3CH=CHCH=CHCOOH}$.

The main functional group is –COOH, so numbering starts from the carbon of the carboxylic acid group.

Numbering from the –COOH side gives:

$$\mathrm{HOOC-CH=CH-CH=CH-CH_3}$$

The carbon chain has 6 carbon atoms, so the parent name is based on hexanoic acid.

There are two double bonds at positions 2 and 4.

So the IUPAC name is Hexa-2,4-dienoic acid.

Final Answer: $$\boxed{\text{Hexa-2,4-dienoic acid}}$$

Hence, the correct option is B.
